confirmed.title: React Aria date field in Sift: month and day are both named 'Reservation date', year is named 'yyyy', and all three boxes show 'Empty'

confirmed.evidence: The CDP AX tree of Sift's view has spinbutton 'Reservation date' value=0, spinbutton 'Reservation date' value=0, spinbutton 'yyyy' value=0, then button 'Book'. Sift shows them as three stacked boxes, each with the visible text 'Empty', under the labels 'Reservation date', 'Reservation date' and 'yyyy'. A sighted user cannot tell which box is the month and which is the day, and a screen reader says 'Reservation date' twice. On the original, the segments have aria-label 'month, ', 'day, ' and 'year, ', each labelled by itself plus the field label, so they read as 'month, Reservation date' and so on, and they show inline as mm/dd/yyyy. Screenshot: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-5/research/shots/r11t5-ariadate.png. The round 10 skeptic already noted the 'Empty' labels, so this is not new.
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9465 SIFT_TAB=T5-amazon-gmail-a11y bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r11t5/axnames.ts http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r10skep-ariadate.html 6000 prints the three spinbuttons with those names. Then: bun /home/nico/projects/sift-test-5/scripts/act.ts shot:ariadate.
confirmed.suspectedCause: Unverified lead: when Sift builds a field's label from aria-labelledby, it seems to drop the segment's own aria-label ('month, ', 'day, ') that a self-reference in aria-labelledby brings in. It also shows aria-valuetext ('Empty') as the visible value instead of the placeholder text (mm, dd, yyyy).
confirmed.verdict:
Confirmed, medium severity. I reproduced it twice on http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r10skep-ariadate.html, after a 6 s wait and again after 15 s. Sift's AX tree has spinbutton 'Reservation date', spinbutton 'Reservation date' and spinbutton 'yyyy', each with value 0. Each box shows the visible text 'Empty'. My screenshot is /home/nico/projects/sift-test-5/research/shots/skep-ariadate-sift.png. With Sift off, the original's AX tree reads 'month, Reservation date', 'day, Reservation date' and 'year, Reservation date', drawn inline as 'mm / dd / yyyy' (/home/nico/projects/sift-test-5/research/shots/skep-ariadate-orig.png). So month and day cannot be told apart in Sift, by sight or by screen reader. Neither the rejected lists nor F1041 cover the duplicate names; the round 10 skeptic only mentioned 'Empty' in passing.

The cause is not what the reporter suspected. A MutationObserver on page load showed that React Aria first inserts each segment with aria-labelledby pointing at an id that does not exist (':r6: :r1:'). About 40 ms later it rewrites the attribute to the segment's own id (':r5: :r1:'). Sift extracted in between, and it never re-reads after that change, because 'aria-labelledby' is not in the observer's attributeFilter (src/content/index.ts:2666). When I forced a re-extraction by appending a few words to a paragraph, the names became 'mm Reservation date', 'dd Reservation date' and 'yyyy Reservation date'. A static copy of the same DOM served from my scratchpad gives the same three names at once. So there is a second, smaller bug. idrefText in src/content/dom.ts reads a referenced node's innerText ('mm'), not its aria-label ('month, '), which the accessible-name algorithm uses for a self-reference. The visible 'Empty' comes from app.tsx's spinbutton case, which renders f.valueText (aria-valuetext) in place of the page's shown text.
confirmed.fix: (1) In src/content/index.ts at line 2666, add 'aria-labelledby', 'aria-label' and 'id' to the MutationObserver attributeFilter. Then names a page fixes after mount get re-read. (2) In idrefText in src/content/dom.ts, use a referenced node's own aria-label when it has one, which covers the element referencing itself, and fall back to innerText otherwise. That gives 'month, Reservation date'. (3) In the spinbutton case of src/content/ui/app.tsx (around line 345), show the page's own text (for example a new 'shown' field set from textIn(el) in toField in generic.ts: 'mm', or '7') as the visible content. Keep aria-valuetext for screen readers only.

confirmed.title: Extraction became quadratic on long runs of same-length siblings: core-budget freezes the page for minutes (new marqueeCopies)
confirmed.where: http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/core-budget.html (6000 comment divs, each with Reply/Like); src/content/extract/generic.ts marqueeCopies (lines 3885-3903), called from the child walk at ~3861
confirmed.evidence: I ran extraction-only bundles on the same page, one after the other, in the same headless Chrome. Round 10 code (scratchpad r10t6/r10.js): 3693/2751 ms. Merged src (r11t6/r11.js): 126567/112078 ms. The outline is identical. Scaling the comments: 1000 comments 1187 -> 5952 ms, 2000 comments 2939 -> 10258 ms. No other fixture out of 164 got slower than 2x. In the extension, Sift on: page.goto took 218 s to reach domcontentloaded, and the original and Sift both first answered at 387 s (one unresponsive gap of 169 s). scripts/firstpaint.ts gives -1/-1 because the page does not answer within its 15 s. The same page with Sift switched off: first content at 2.4 s. A Chrome running the round 10 base build (sift-r10-base built into scratchpad, port 9486): 23.0 s and 21.4 s. CPU profile of one extract(): 85.5 s self time in key() inside marqueeCopies, plus 15.1 s in querySelectorAll called from key(), plus 7.1 s in the \s+ regex.
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9466 ./scripts/chrome.sh start; SIFT_PORT=9466 SIFT_TAB=T6-fixtures bun scripts/firstpaint.ts http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/core-budget.html "article p" 1 -> 'original -1 ms, sift -1 ms' (the page is frozen). Without the extension: cd /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r11t6 && bun prof.ts http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/core-budget.html r11.js (about 2 minutes, prints the profile) and bun scale.ts 1000 2000 (round 10 bundle against the merged one)
confirmed.suspectedCause: marqueeCopies (added for F1001) groups siblings by text length. For each sibling whose length equals an earlier one's, it calls key() on every earlier same-length sibling: textContent + regex + querySelectorAll('a[href]'), with no caching. 6000 comments that differ only in their number mostly share one length, so the cost is O(n^2) key builds. Fix lead: compute each element's key once (a Map, or a Set of keys per length) and only then compare; or skip the check past a small sibling count, since a marquee repeats a short strip.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, high severity, and a regression. I built two extract-only bundles of my own: one from HEAD 0b07e6b and one from 7315d9a, the round 10 base, which has no marqueeCopies. I timed extract() in a plain headless Chrome with no extension. On fx/core-budget.html the base took 2401 and 2131 ms. HEAD took 88527 and 85590 ms. Both produced the same model, 1139796 bytes. Generated pages with N comments, base vs HEAD: 500 comments 327 vs 847 ms, 1000 comments 618 vs 3165 ms, 2000 comments 1103 vs 6613 ms. Growth follows the number of same-length siblings: comments 1000-5999 all have the same text length. I patched a scratch copy so each sibling's key() is computed once. That brought the fixture back to 3460 and 2731 ms, so marqueeCopies is the cause. In the extension on port 9466 with Sift on, firstpaint.ts printed -1/-1. My longer-timeout poll got domcontentloaded at 113.8 s. One evaluate call was blocked for 113 s. The original and Sift both first answered at 226.9 s.
confirmed.fix: src/content/extract/generic.ts marqueeCopies (~3885): build key() once per element and keep a Set<string> of keys per text length. Then each sibling is one key build plus one Set lookup instead of a scan of every earlier same-length sibling with key() rebuilt on both sides. Optionally skip the check when ks is long (more than ~50 siblings), since a marquee repeats a short strip.

confirmed.verdict:
Confirmed, high. I used Chrome 9469 with a copy of the reporter's mock. doors.html with 'Doors open at 19:30.' made 1 call. I then changed the file to say 20:00. The revisit made 0 calls and the Short version still said 'Doors open at 19:30.', while the page (curl) says 20:00. A worse case is mine: I added a two-word line,

Concert cancelled.

. The revisit made 0 calls and the Short version did not mention the cancellation. Offline, t/stable.ts shows the same cache-key text for all 4 edits. The old time passes the number check only because '30' appears elsewhere on the page. Without the other '30', checked() drops the sentence and the time is just missing. Within one visit, doorslive.html at 16 s showed both 'Doors open at 19:30.' and the new 'Doors open at 20:00. The start is delayed…'. The reuse path has the same gap: my reuse2.ts renumbers [[B1]] to [[B2]] and changes the time, and reuseShort still returns the old 19:30 text.
confirmed.fix: src/background/text.ts stableText: keep every prose line that has no link in the key, including short ones. Drop a line only when it is nothing but a label once its time or count is removed ('Updated 10:32', '5 min ago', '1,2 M views'). Never drop it just for having 2 words or fewer. textLines inherits the fix. Make the same change to `counts` in src/content/short.ts, so a changed short line gets a change hash and staleAbout can drop the old sentence.

Then the language is named to the model, which outranks the system prompt's 'never translate'. When a reliable detection of the text differs from the page's lang, name the detected language, or name none and keep 'Same language as the text'.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, high, regression. In the code, entryLang(text, 'en', detect) returns the page language whenever the detected language (pl/sv/tr/id) has no FUNCTION_WORDS list. t/wantlang.ts prints want='en' for each of them. The Polish article got a Short version in English: 'After a debate lasting over six hours, opposition members accused the mayor of excessive debt…'. condenseFits(out, 'en') then accepts it, and it is cached.
confirmed.fix: src/background/text.ts entryLang (as used by condenseLang in src/background/index.ts:756): when a reliable detection of the long prose differs from the page lang, return the detected language even if it has no word list. Or return '' so the prompt names no language and the 'Same language as the text' rule decides. Name a language only when the page lang and a reliable detection agree, or detection is unreliable.

confirmed.where: src/background/text.ts:310 (NUMBER_WORDS covers only en/es/pt/fr/de/it), :580 (sourceNumbers), :824 (dropUnsupported drops the sentence)
confirmed.evidence: I captured Sift's exact condense prompt for fx pl2.html (lang="pl") with the mock, then sent it once to the last-resort model (openai/gpt-6-luna; the main model answered 402). The answer was faithful and wrote numbers as digits: 'Rada miasta przyjęła budżet na 2027 rok stosunkiem głosów 20 do 9.', 'Bilety … zdrożeją od stycznia o 10 proc.', 'Miasto chce za to kupić 40 autobusów…', '…w życie 1 stycznia…' and 'Dochody mają wynieść około 4 mld zł.' The source spells these out (dwudziestu, dziewięciu, dziesięć, czterdzieści, pierwszego, czterech). Sift's checks (r11ai/t/plcheck.ts) drop all five sentences as 'number'. The vote, the fare rise and the buses are gone, and nothing puts them back. The same happens for Catalan, Dutch, Swedish, Russian and any other language whose number words are not listed.
confirmed.repro: bun scratchpad/r11ai/t/plcheck.ts (uses r11ai/last-condense.json and raw-pl.txt). In Chrome: mock running, settings.ts mock, then bun scratchpad/r11ai/watch.ts pl2.html 7.
confirmed.suspectedCause: sourceNumbers knows number words in six languages only, so a digit the model writes for a Polish number word counts as invented, and the whole sentence goes. Lead: when the page language has no number-word list, do not drop a sentence for 'number' alone. Or put the source sentence back, as warningOf does for warnings.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed. I rate it medium to high. NUMBER_WORDS covers only en/es/pt/fr/de/it. In Chrome 9469, the mock replayed the captured real model answer for pl2.html (lang=pl). resp.json is an authentic OpenRouter gpt-6-luna response. The 'KRÓTKA WERSJA' starts at 'Po debacie…', and the vote '20 do 9', the 10% fare rise, the 40 buses, '1 stycznia' and '4 mld zł' are all dropped. t/plcheck.ts drops those 5 sentences as 'number'. The source spells them dwudziestu, dziewięciu, dziesięć, czterdzieści, pierwszego and czterech. My own real run on the lang=en Polish page (N1) lost the same lead facts: its English Short version has no vote count, fare rise or buses. How often this happens depends on how often a source spells numbers out. When it does, the article's key facts disappear silently.
confirmed.fix: src/background/text.ts unsupported/dropUnsupported: when the source is in a language with no NUMBER_WORDS list, do not drop a sentence for 'number' alone. Pass the language in, or detect it by the source having number-like words that wordNumbers cannot read. Alternatively, put the source sentence back the way warningOf does, or extend NUMBER_WORDS to more languages.

confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, medium, regression.
